name: Web Recon
summary: Fingerprints web pages: favicon hashes in the forms Shodan, Censys and other search services index, HHHash of the response header names, and a hash of the HTML tag structure. Desktop only.
description:
Fingerprints of web pages to pivot on: the favicon a site serves, the order of its response header names, and the tag structure of its HTML. Operators rotate domains, IP addresses and certificates but tend to reuse what sits underneath: a phishing kit's favicon, a server stack's header layout, a storefront template's markup. A fingerprint shared by otherwise unrelated hosts is a lead for clustering them (Tor and clear web, staging and production, a clone and its original).

## Plugins

All three run on URL nodes (`web.url`, read from `url`), create one fingerprint node per URL linked from it, and need the desktop app.

| Plugin | Requests | Creates | Edge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Favicon Hash | `/favicon.ico` on the URL's host | `web.favicon_hash` | `has favicon` |
| HTTP Header Hash (HHHash) | the URL itself, over HTTP/1.1 | `web.hhhash` | `has header hash` |
| DOM Structure Hash | the URL itself | `web.dom_hash` | `has dom hash` |

A fingerprint node is identified by its hash, so the same hash found on several URLs is one node with an edge from each: that shared node is the pivot. A re-run refreshes the existing node instead of adding a copy, and the run summary says whether each hash was new or already in the graph. A URL whose request fails is counted and skipped without stopping the run.

### Favicon Hash

`run.vineyard.plugins.favicon_hash`

Fetches `/favicon.ico` from the host of each selected URL and hashes the file in every form the search services index, each under its own property of one node:

| Property | Form | Searched on |
|---|---|---|
| `hash_value` | MurmurHash3 x86 32-bit (seed 0) of the file's base64, with a newline every 76 characters and at the end, as a signed decimal | Shodan `http.favicon.hash`, FOFA `icon_hash`, Censys `favicons.hash_shodan`, ZoomEye `iconhash` |
| `mmh3_hex` | `hash_value` in hex, sign kept (`-30149ea`) | Criminal IP `favicon:` |
| `md5` | MD5 of the file's bytes, lowercase hex | Censys `favicons.hash_md5`, ZoomEye `iconhash`, 360 Quake `favicon`, Hunter.how `favicon_hash`, ONYPHE `app.favicon.imagemd5`, VirusTotal `main_icon_md5` |
| `sha256` | SHA-256 of the file's bytes, lowercase hex | Censys `favicons.hash_sha256`, Netlas `http.favicon.hash_sha256`, urlscan.io `hash` |
| `phash` | pHash of the decoded image, as the Python ImageHash library computes it | Censys indexes a 64-bit perceptual hash as `favicons.hash_phash` but does not document its algorithm, so a match is not established |
| `dhash` | Krawetz's dHash of the decoded image, in the bit order VirusTotal's appears to use | VirusTotal `main_icon_dhash`, a similarity search |

The node also records `hash_algorithm` (`mmh3`), `favicon_url` and `observed_at`.

- `phash` and `dhash` are perceptual: they stay close when an icon is re-encoded, resized or slightly edited. Two values are compared by how many of their 64 bits differ (Krawetz counts 10 or fewer as a likely variant), not by equality.
- Both reproduce Pillow's decoding and Lanczos resize bit for bit, because ImageHash runs on Pillow. They are computed for ICO, PNG and BMP icons, except 16-bit grayscale PNG, 16-bit and RLE BMP, icons over 2048 pixels a side, and files Pillow refuses; such an icon still gets the other four hashes. For a multi-image ICO the frame is Pillow's choice: the largest, and among equal sizes the lowest colour depth.
- `phash` also reproduces SciPy's DCT. On a mirrored or smoothly shaded icon some bits come down to rounding noise that depends on the SciPy build: the value matches SciPy up to 1.17 on x86-64, while SciPy 1.18 and arm64 builds can differ in those bits.
- VirusTotal does not document its `main_icon_dhash` algorithm. This one follows the icon dHash of SuperPeHasher and FileInsight-plugins; with it, Facebook's favicon comes within 2 bits of the value a third-party VirusTotal query list (https://github.com/repulsivityy/vt_dorks) gives for it. VirusTotal's own documented example could not be reproduced.
- Netlas's `perceptual_hash` is an aHash and is not computed.
- Only `/favicon.ico` is fetched. The page is not read for a `<link rel="icon">`, and a redirect is not followed: it counts as a failed fetch.
- The download is capped at 512 KB; a larger icon counts as a failed fetch. Censys hashes only the first 384 KB of a favicon, so for an icon larger than that none of its Censys hashes match these.
- A common default icon (a framework's, a hosting panel's) matches unrelated sites.

### HTTP Header Hash (HHHash)

`run.vineyard.plugins.hhhash`

Sends a GET to each selected URL over HTTP/1.1 and computes its HHHash (https://github.com/adulau/HHHash): `hhh:1:` followed by the SHA-256 of the response header names, in the order the server sent them, joined with `:`. It is computed the way the reference `hhhash` Python package does, so values compare with other tools': HTTP/1.1 (HTTP/2 lowercases names), redirects not followed, the request headers that client sends (`Accept: */*`, `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate`), a repeated name such as `Set-Cookie` counted once at its first position, and names kept in their original case.

- **Node properties:** `hash_value`, `header_count`, `server_hint` (the `Server` header, when sent) and `observed_at`.
- Any status is fingerprinted, 403 and 404 included: an error page still shows the stack.
- Header structure reflects the server stack (web server, reverse proxy, framework defaults), so the same HHHash points at the same deployment practice.

### DOM Structure Hash

`run.vineyard.plugins.dom_hash`

Fetches the HTML of each selected URL, takes the names of its tags in document order, joins them with `|` and keeps the first 32 hex characters of their SHA-256: the dom-hash technique from The Art of Pivoting. Text and attributes do not count, so a template keeps its hash when its text, branding or language change, and cloned storefronts, phishing kits and leak sites built on one template cluster together.

- **Node properties:** `hash_value`, `tag_count` and `observed_at`.
- Tags are read with a regular expression over the source, not a full HTML parser: good enough to cluster templates, but malformed HTML can give a slightly different sequence than a parser would.
- The page is capped at 2 MB. A status of 400 or above, or a page with no tags, counts as a failed fetch. Redirects are not followed.

## Requirements

- **Desktop app only.** The targets are arbitrary sites, and reading a cross-origin body or its headers needs CORS headers that most sites do not send. The desktop app sends the requests from its main process; in the web app the plugins say so and stop.
- No API key or account, and no Vineyard-operated service.

## What it contacts

- **Active:** every plugin requests the selected site directly from the analyst's machine, one request per URL. Favicon Hash requests `/favicon.ico` on the URL's host; HHHash and DOM Structure Hash request the URL itself. The site sees each request.
- Requests are anonymous, with no cookies or credentials, and do not follow redirects.
- No third-party service is queried. The hashes are computed in the app; the search services named above are where they can be looked up, separately.

## Data and licences

The pack ships and downloads no data set: every value is computed from the site's own response.

## Source

https://github.com/Vineyard-Intelligence/pluginpack-web-recon (Apache-2.0)

`dist/pack.mjs` is built from `src/` with a pinned esbuild, so the published bundle can be checked against the source: `node build.mjs && git diff --exit-code dist/pack.mjs`.

`test-plugin.mjs` checks the plugins against values from the reference implementations: Python's `mmh3` for the Shodan form, Pillow and ImageHash for `phash` and `dhash` (on the reference icons `test-fixtures/make-favicons.py` writes), and the value the `hhhash` package publishes for its own example.
